title: Audit the operating file
learning_outcome: Audit the full workflow, identify the weakest gate, and decide whether to keep, shrink, or retire it.
exercise: Present the Operating File with missing evidence made visible and an explicit human disposition.

scenes.narration_exact: “At the end of Harbor's fictional Friday, Morgan has a full Operating File. It contains a job, sources, receipts, authority limits, a team handoff, evaluation cases, a proof outline, a research proposal, and a six-beat rehearsal. The file is impressive in one sense: its gaps are visible. Staffing is still unconfirmed. Spend is unapproved. The research test has not run. The board proof has not been shared. The capstone asks whether this design deserves to continue, in what smaller form, and under whose care.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Chapter Twenty-Six names five operating questions: route, log, gate, memory, review. Who receives the work? What record explains it? Where does a human decide? What may be remembered, and by whom? When will someone revisit the rule? The companion workbook expands these into an Accountability Stack from source through rollback. We will use the larger worksheet to audit the single Harbor workflow, while keeping the five questions as a readable spine.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Finish with export and rollback. The proof outline is scoped to an audience and remains `not shared`. If a claim is wrong, Harbor can retain the prior draft, correct the paper brief, and record the reason. If a local rule later causes harm, a named owner must be able to narrow, revoke, or retire it. The weakest gate today is staffing confirmation: without it, the brief cannot become a team proposal. That is a useful result, even though nothing launches.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Present your Operating File as a one-page audit. Walk source, event, proposal, memory, routing, action, approval, cost, export, and rollback. For each layer, write owner, evidence, privacy tier, gate, failure mode, and next improvement. Mark missing evidence openly. Then write a human disposition field with decision, owner, date, reason, and next review date. You may leave the decision pending. This is a design review: do not deploy, publish, spend, contact anyone, or run an agent because a worksheet is complete.”
scenes.on_screen_copy_exact: Exercise card below; 3:20 quiet writing timer with optional pause.
scenes.exercise_prompt_exact: Complete an `Accountability Stack` for the workflow you designed across L01–L15. For each of source, event, proposal, memory, routing, action, approval, cost/spend, export, and rollback, record owner, evidence reference, privacy tier, approval gate, failure mode, and next improvement. Identify the weakest gate. Add a disposition with `keep`, `shrink`, `retire`, or `pending`; named human owner; decision date; reason; next review date; and unresolved evidence. If the human has not decided, leave date blank and status `pending`. This exercise does not authorize a run.
